summary:
The narrowed design answers or explicitly hands off every earlier finding:

- **Scanner fixes:**
  - The skip goes into a separate skippedStores list and never into topLevel.unreadable, and the report carries counts only (M5/X1).
  - The open seam guards and counts opens, with a single call site (m4).
  - Paths are resolved via the final path, without GetFullPath on popped paths, and the store's parent is opened, never the store (m1/m2/Y5).
  - NotScanned rows get no 'Show in Explorer' (Y6).
  - The rules carry a literal (?m), case-insensitive scoped groups and a RunAs rule (N7/Y2).
- **Protocol fixes:**
  - The pre-restart reading is Rpre, and -Protocol refuses to start on an old boot (X4).
  - The guard is per arm and records guardAtStart (R4-2).
  - Completeness is checked against a plan line, with acted/Cancelled checks and INCOMPLETE on null inputs (M1, R2-R3-3, m7).
  - The fltmc paste only counts with its header line (R2-N3).
  - Shut down is recorded as sourced, not measured (N4).
- **Moot or handed off:** the dir arms, ScanArm, -Attribute and the store-size walk are dropped with reasons that hold now the current boot is post-Restart. The verdict-related items go to SC-128 by ID.

Five problems remain:

1. **The workaround switch contradicts Q-182 (major).** The new switch's off position lifts the picked-root refusal. The person explicitly decided refusal with no user override. The design raises the conflict as an open question but builds one side anyway. The 'project rule' behind the whole Settings stack is also not cited.
2. **The 2 GiB per-arm guard will likely kill the one cold full-scan measurement (major).**
   - The design says this guard lets 'no guard stop on any arm' be met, but its own figures contradict that.
   - Arm L reached more than 513 MiB and was cut off at 3.31M entries.
   - At the cited ~1 KB per first-time open, SizeProbe on about 2.3M files adds roughly 2.2 GiB.
   - So the first exe-full scan, the only cold full-scan measurement SC-128 needs, is likely killed, and the Restart session reads INCOMPLETE.
3. **Transfer invariant 3 is marked 'holds' on a walk that was cut short (minor).** Nothing states that arm L reached the store and skipped it before the guard stopped it.
4. **Nothing tests the open-seam backstop when it is bypassed (minor).** So a broken backstop would read 0 forever.
5. **The unattended -Rehearse gate may flake (minor).** It runs cancel triggers against a 2,000-folder tree that may finish before a trigger fires.

Separately: spike #87's per-mark logs, which DONE (a)'s L figures and the outcome-C decision rest on, exist only under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. The risk-spike stage should have committed them.

findings.claim: The new 'wcifs-layer-store' switch governs both the C: exclusion and the picked-root refusal. Unticking it, after a confirmation, lets the user scan the store as picked. That contradicts answered Q-182: the design itself says Q-182 'refuses with no user override' and 'explicitly overrode user's choice wins'. The design raises the conflict as an open question, then builds one branch of it anyway (case 7: 'the picked root scanned as picked'), which is proceeding as though the open question were answered. The rule cited as forcing the switch ('the project's rule that a workaround for an outside defect is a per-bug setting, on by default') has no Q-number or file reference anywhere in the design, unlike every other rule it relies on. Yet it brings in a Settings window, a confirmation window, a new hook mode, two window cases, a report field and a fitness rule.
findings.evidence: Key decision 2: 'Its off position restores the plain scan exactly: the store is walked, and a picked root inside it is scanned as picked.' Coherence check 3: 'Q-182 refuses with no user override; the rule needs a per-bug switch whose off position restores the plain behaviour.' Open question 1. Case 7: 'the picked root scanned as picked'.
findings.fix: Until the person answers the open question, build only what both decisions agree on. The switch governs the C: exclusion. The Refused outcome stays unconditional, as Q-182 decided. Change case 7 to assert 'off: store listed and counted; picked root still Refused'. Cite in the design record where the per-bug workaround rule lives. If it cannot be cited, keep the KnownWorkarounds list but drop the off position for now.

findings.claim: The per-arm guard (combined pool growth over the arm's /before above 2 GiB) is justified as the value that 'lets the request's no guard stop on any arm actually be met by a real session'. The design's own figures say it will not be. Arm L, listing only, reached +513 MiB and was cut off at 3.31M entries, so a full listing costs more than that. A cold exe-full scan adds SizeProbe opens on 'about 2.3M+ files'. The cited 25H2 source measured about 1 KB of pool per first-time path open, which is roughly 2.2 GiB more. So the first exe-full of the post-Restart session is likely killed. That is the only cold full-app measurement in the session and the one figure SC-128 most needs. The 3-4 hour session then reads RUN INCOMPLETE. Decidable disagreement 1 admits this ('If it is over, the first exe-full of every session reads INCOMPLETE') while the selection rationale claims the opposite.
findings.evidence: Key decision 8 rationale: 'L alone (listing only, cut off at 3.31M entries) reached +513 MiB combined.' Decidable disagreement 1: 'A full exe scan adds SizeProbe on about 2.3M+ files, which nobody has measured cold.' learn.microsoft.com/en-nz/answers/questions/5966064: '3,000 first-time opens cost about 1 KB of pool per path.' Selection rationale: 'so that the request's no guard stop on any arm can actually be met by a real session'.
findings.fix: Keep the real machine protection (Available MBytes under 3 GiB) and raise the per-arm pool ceiling for exe arms to a figure above the predicted cold cost, for example 6 GiB, stated with this arithmetic. Alternatively, drop the 'can be met' claim, and have -Report print a guard-stopped first exe-full's /exit net and list it as 'stopped by guard at <bytes>', so the truncated cold cost is still logged.

findings.claim: Cross-domain invariant 3 ('a full C: walk with the exclusion reaches no live WCI entry, including through Containers' siblings and C:\Users\All Users') is marked 'holds' on the evidence of spike #87's arm L. But L was not a full walk: the guard cut it off at 3.31M entries. The design never says L had reached and skipped the store before then. If the depth-first order had not reached ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Containers, then 'no WC* rise, underStore=0' says nothing about the store's siblings, All Users or the exclusion itself. Decidable disagreement 3 (would_force_resynthesis: true) leans on the same evidence.
findings.evidence: cross_domain_transfer invariant 3: status 'holds', evidence 'Spike #87... arm L, a cold C: listing with the store excluded, had no WC* rise and underStore=0'. Key decision 8: 'L alone (listing only, cut off at 3.31M entries)'.
findings.fix: Read spike #87's L.json for a skippedStores entry, or the folder count at which the store was skipped, and state in the record whether L passed the store. If that cannot be shown, mark invariant 3 must-verify. The person-run exe-full arms (notScanned ≥ 1, raw WC* per arm) can then settle it, with the record updated from that session's logs.

findings.claim: The open-seam backstop's only stated evidence is 'opensUnderExcludedStore 0' in case 1 and in the exe-full arms. That is exactly what a backstop that never refuses, or never counts, would also show. No case drives OpenDirectory with an active rule on a path under a planted store, to show it refuses before CreateFileW, returns the skip outcome and counts 1. Without that, the 'independent tripwire' (m4) could be broken and still read 0 forever.
findings.evidence: Component 'Open-seam guard and count': 'the count is 0 unless something bypasses it. That makes the count an independent tripwire.' Cases 1-7 test only the descent path. The 'backstop called directly' case from the earlier design is gone.
findings.fix: Add a Core test that calls DirectoryReader.Read (or OpenDirectory) with the active rule on a path under a planted store. Deny-ACL that store, so an open that was actually issued would return access-denied instead of the skip. Assert the skip outcome and opensUnderExcludedStore = 1.

findings.claim: -Rehearse runs unattended at validate and must read RUN COMPLETE. Its four cancel arms and one close arm need an '^acted ' line, a foldersAtCancel value and status Cancelled. They run against a generated tree of about 2,000 folders and 10,000 files, which a scan can finish in about a second. If the hook's folder-count trigger is polled more slowly than the scan runs, it logs 'ended before the trigger' or the deadline refusal (StartupHook.cs:653/:665). The rehearsal then reads INCOMPLETE because of timing, not because -Protocol is broken, and validate flakes.
findings.evidence: PoolWatch component: '-Rehearse runs the same code over a generated %TEMP% tree (about 2,000 folders and 10,000 files), with 60 s / 30 s windows and folder-count triggers'. -Report: 'an exe-cancel or exe-close with no '^acted ' line or no foldersAtCancel... counts as not acted'.
findings.fix: Size the rehearsal tree so a scan lasts at least 10× the hook's trigger poll interval. Set the folder triggers at 25% or less of the tree's folders. Have PoolWatchCases print the hook's refused line when the rehearsal is INCOMPLETE, so a timing flake can be told apart from a harness defect.

dimensions_checked.result: F2: the 2 GiB per-arm guard is claimed to make 'no guard stop' reachable, but the design's own numbers (L over 513 MiB when cut off; about 1 KB per cold open on about 2.3M files) predict the first exe-full trips it. F3: invariant 3 is marked 'holds' on a walk cut off at 3.31M entries. The excluded-bytes premise is now correctly marked 'fails' and is disclosed under Q-180/Q-181.

F5: the rehearsal's cancel triggers race a scan of a tiny tree. Resolve's error cases (workaround off, store or parent absent, final-path failure, root unopenable) and the sibling cases ('Layers.', 'Layers ', Layers2) are covered. Loopback SMB is documented as a gap.

none: the store is enforced twice by construction (FolderDone and the single OpenDirectory call site), and the switch is read in one place under a fitness rule. The completeness check against the plan line closes the silent pass on missing arms.

The KnownWorkarounds/Settings/confirmation stack is proportionate only if the uncited per-bug workaround rule exists. That question and the Q-182 conflict are raised under F1. PoolWatch is otherwise lean: no verdict code, no ScanArm, no pressure step or drift model.

none beyond F1: Resolve, the Refused outcome, the open-seam refusal, the report additions (counts only, never in topLevel.unreadable), and the -Report exit codes and INCOMPLETE reasons are all specified.

Null inputs, missing marks, guardStop and guardAtStart cascades, and refused hook outcomes all read INCOMPLETE with the arm named. Gap in the stage record: spike #87's marks.jsonl, events.log and L.json, which the outcome-C narrowing and DONE (a)'s L figures rest on, exist only under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and may not be readable by the ordinary-user build. The risk-spike stage should have committed them under docs/design/SL-095-runs/. The design states this gap.

F1: the switch's off position contradicts answered Q-182 and builds one branch of an open question. Every earlier accepted-pending finding is either answered (M5/X1, m1, m2, m4, m5, m7, N4, N7/Y2, X4, Y5, Y6, M1-harness, R2-R3-3, R2-N3, R4-2), moot after the narrowing (X3, R2-N2, N5, N6, R3-2, R2-N1), or handed to SC-128 by ID (M2, M3/N3/X2, M4/Y1, M6/N2/X5, R3-1, R4-1, Y3, the m6 trigger).

Rules use a literal (?m) plus scoped (?i:), are twinned and planted, and update the RuleCases pins (Q-085). App changes trigger WindowMutants -Mutant All (Q-114). Report fields are counts and ids only (Q-016). Rule 4's quote-then-token pattern may also fire on comments in PoolWatch.ps1. That is friction the plants will expose, not a defect.

F4: no test drives the open-seam refusal directly. Otherwise there are planted-store Core tests for cases 1-7 (never skipped), WindowCases for the notScanned report, the refused root and the settings toggles, PoolWatchCases fixtures for completeness and no verdict tokens, and -Rehearse end to end.

none: the store override is internal and kept out of the App and rigs by rule. The report carries no paths. PoolWatch is guarded against RunAs. The off switch, which enables a kernel leak, sits behind a confirmation that states the consequence; whether it should exist at all is F1.
